28|    """
29|    Generate a personalized greeting.
30|
31|    Args:

41|def add_numbers(a: int, b: int) -> int:
42|    """
43|    Add two numbers together.
44|
45|    Args:
46|        a: First number
47|        b: Second number
48|
49|    Returns:
50|        The sum of a and b
51|    """

54|
55|def create_agent():
56|    """Create and return the agent (ensures env vars are loaded first)."""
57|    api_key = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")

59|        raise ValueError("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not found. Please set it in .env file.")

62|        client_args={
63|            "api_key": api_key,
64|        },
65|        model_id="claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929",
66|        max_tokens=1024,
67|    )
68|
69|    return Agent(
70|        model=model,
71|        tools=[greet, add_numbers],
72|        system_prompt="You are a friendly assistant that helps users with greetings and simple math.",
73|    )

1|"""``RunLedger`` -- the durable run ledger core (ADR 0010, plan §5-§6).
2|
3|Implements ADR 0010 crash boundaries 1-7 (Node-side boundaries 8-11 are out
4|of scope). Every mutation is a strictly conditional write against the
5|injected ``CoordinationStore``/``ContentStore`` ports; nothing here calls
6|``time.time()`` (an injected ``Clock`` drives every timestamp/expiry
7|decision) or imports an LLM provider SDK.
8|
9|Run-state changes always go through ``src/contracts/states.py::
10|is_legal_transition`` ("run" machine): an illegal transition raises
11|``IllegalRunTransition`` rather than being silently applied. Durable stage
12|records are always validated through ``StageRecordV1``
13|(``src/contracts/audit.py``) before being persisted.
14|
15|Phase 3.4 additive methods (``src/alr_run``, flagged for supervisor review):
16|``get_completed_manifest`` (pure read of the B6 completion record, used for
17|idempotent-replay detection) and ``fail_run`` (the missing ``RUNNING ->
18|analysis_incomplete|failed`` terminal transition -- no prior method reached
19|those two states). Both are pure additions; no existing method's behaviour

FILE: run_ledger_ports (5007B) — /tmp/denuto/src/run_ledger/ports.py
1|"""Storage ports for the durable run ledger (ADR 0010: "Authority split").
2|
3|Two ports model the split authority the ADR requires:
4|
5|- ``CoordinationStore`` -- DynamoDB-shaped coordination truth. Every mutation
6|  is strictly conditional (``put_if_absent`` / ``update_if``); there is no
7|  unconditional write on this port at all, so a caller can never silently
8|  clobber concurrent state.
9|- ``ContentStore`` -- immutable, versioned content truth. Objects are
10|  content-addressed where the plan's object layout says so
11|  (``put_content``) or write-once at a fixed path (``put_if_none_match``);
12|  there is deliberately no delete or overwrite operation on this port --
13|  supersession is always a new object plus a new coordination head.
14|
15|``Clock`` is a third, tiny port: ``now_ms()`` only. Ledger logic (see
16|``ledger.py`` / ``audit_chain.py``) never calls ``time.time()`` directly so
17|lease/expiry/backoff behaviour is deterministic under test.
18|"""
19|
20|from __future__ import annotations
21|
22|from collections.abc import Mapping
23|from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
24|
25|__all__ = [
26|    "Clock",
27|    "ConditionFailed",
28|    "ContentStore",
29|    "CoordinationStore",
30|    "ObjectAlreadyExists",
31|]
32|
33|
34|class ConditionFailed(Exception):
35|    """A ``CoordinationStore`` conditional write lost the race.
36|
37|    Carries the item currently stored at ``key`` (``None`` when the key does
38|    not exist, e.g. an ``update_if`` against a never-created key) so callers
39|    can decide idempotent-return vs. hard failure without a second read.
40|    """
41|
42|    def __init__(self, key: str, current: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> None:
43|        self.key = key
44|        self.current = current
45|        super().__init__(f"condition failed for key {key!r}")
46|
47|
48|class ObjectAlreadyExists(Exception):
49|    """A ``ContentStore.put_if_none_match`` call found the path already written."""
50|
51|    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
52|        self.path = path
53|        super().__init__(f"object already exists at path {path!r}")
54|
55|
56|@runtime_checkable
57|class Clock(Protocol):
58|    """Injected time source. ``ledger.py``/``audit_chain.py`` never read wall-clock time."""
59|
60|    def now_ms(self) -> int:
61|        """Current time in epoch milliseconds, as understood by the caller's clock."""
62|        ...
63|
64|
65|@runtime_checkable
66|class CoordinationStore(Protocol):
67|    """DynamoDB-shaped coordination truth: conditional writes only.
68|
69|    Every stored item is a plain mapping the caller controls, including its
70|    own ``"revision"`` string field where the ledger uses one as a
71|    compare-and-swap token (``StageRecordV1.revision`` is the contract
72|    example; internal ledger records follow the same convention). ``get``
73|    is a consistent read: it always reflects the most recently applied
74|    conditional write.
75|    """

FILE: run_ledger_retry (1958B) — /tmp/denuto/src/run_ledger/retry.py
1|"""Deterministic per-stage retry budget (ADR 0010: "Retry budgets").
2|
3|Exponential backoff with full jitter, computed from an explicitly passed
4|``random.Random`` -- never the module-global ``random`` functions -- so
5|retry timing is reproducible under test given the same seed/attempt
6|sequence. Exhaustion is a pure function of ``attempt``/``max_attempts``; the
7|ledger (``RunLedger.record_stage_output``) is what durably records the
8|resulting classified failure (``failure_code`` on ``StageRecordV1``).
9|"""
10|
11|from __future__ import annotations
12|
13|import random
14|from dataclasses import dataclass
15|
16|__all__ = ["RetryPolicy"]
17|
18|
19|@dataclass(frozen=True)
20|class RetryPolicy:
21|    """Per-stage attempt cap plus exponential-backoff-with-jitter parameters."""
22|
23|    max_attempts: int
24|    base_delay_ms: int
25|    multiplier: float = 2.0
26|    max_delay_ms: int = 60_000
27|
28|    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
29|        if self.max_attempts < 1:
30|            raise ValueError("max_attempts must be >= 1")
31|        if self.base_delay_ms < 0:
32|            raise ValueError("base_delay_ms must be >= 0")
33|        if self.multiplier <= 0:
34|            raise ValueError("multiplier must be > 0")
35|        if self.max_delay_ms < 0:
36|            raise ValueError("max_delay_ms must be >= 0")
37|
38|    def is_exhausted(self, attempt: int) -> bool:
39|        """True once ``attempt`` (1-based, the attempt that just failed) has used the budget."""
40|        if attempt < 1:
41|            raise ValueError("attempt must be >= 1")
42|        return attempt >= self.max_attempts
43|
44|    def backoff_ms(self, attempt: int, rng: random.Random) -> int:
45|        """Deterministic exponential-backoff-with-full-jitter delay before the attempt after ``attempt``."""
46|        if attempt < 1:
47|            raise ValueError("attempt must be >= 1")
48|        raw = min(float(self.max_delay_ms), self.base_delay_ms * (self.multiplier ** (attempt - 1)))
49|        if raw <= 0:
50|            return 0
51|        return int(rng.uniform(0, raw))

FILE: harness_middleware (7229B) — /tmp/denuto/src/harness/middleware.py
1|"""
2|Composable middleware stack for LLM calls.
3|
4|This module provides the base types for the Denuto harness middleware chain.
5|Middlewares wrap ``invoke_with_fallback`` to enable cross-cutting concerns such
6|as grounding verification, loop detection, cost guarding, and few-shot
7|injection — without modifying the core provider-routing logic.
8|
9|Usage
10|-----
11|Build a stack and pass it to ``invoke_with_fallback``, or set it as the
12|active stack via ``set_middleware_stack`` so it is picked up automatically
13|by every ``invoke_with_fallback`` call within the current context::
14|
15|    from src.harness.middleware import MiddlewareStack, set_middleware_stack
16|    from src.harness.grounding_middleware import GroundingMiddleware
17|    from src.harness.loop_detection_middleware import LoopDetectionMiddleware
18|
19|    stack = MiddlewareStack([LoopDetectionMiddleware(), GroundingMiddleware()])
20|    token = set_middleware_stack(stack)
21|    try:
22|        ...  # all invoke_with_fallback calls in this context use the stack
23|    finally:
24|        _middleware_stack_var.reset(token)
25|
26|Design
27|------
28|- ``MiddlewareContext`` is the single request/response carrier.  Every
29|  middleware receives and returns the same object, mutating it in place.
30|- ``Middleware`` is a structural Protocol — any callable matching the
31|  signature qualifies.
32|- ``MiddlewareStack.execute`` threads the chain: each middleware calls
33|  ``await next(ctx)`` to hand off to the next layer; the innermost ``next``
34|  is the actual LLM handler.
35|"""
36|
37|from __future__ import annotations
38|
39|import contextvars
40|import logging
41|from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
42|from dataclasses import dataclass, field
43|from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
44|
45|logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
46|
47|# Type alias for the "next" callable each middleware receives
48|NextFn = Callable[["MiddlewareContext"], Awaitable["MiddlewareContext"]]
49|
50|# Contextvar holding the active middleware stack for the current request.
51|# Mirrors the pattern used by src/billing/cost_tracker.py.
52|_middleware_stack_var: contextvars.ContextVar[MiddlewareStack | None] = contextvars.ContextVar(
53|    "middleware_stack", default=None
54|)
55|
56|
57|def get_middleware_stack() -> MiddlewareStack | None:
58|    """Return the active middleware stack for the current context, if any."""
59|    return _middleware_stack_var.get(None)
60|
61|
62|def set_middleware_stack(stack: MiddlewareStack | None) -> contextvars.Token:
63|    """Set the active middleware stack for the current context.
64|
65|    Returns the reset token so the caller can restore the previous value::
66|
67|        token = set_middleware_stack(stack)
68|        try:
69|            ...
70|        finally:
71|            _middleware_stack_var.reset(token)
72|    """
73|    return _middleware_stack_var.set(stack)
74|
75|
76|@dataclass
77|class MiddlewareContext:
78|    """Ca

19|
20|def _utc_now_iso() -> str:
21|    """Return a stable UTC timestamp format used by harness state records."""
22|
23|    return datetime.now(UTC).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
24|
25|
26|class HarnessStateManager:
27|    """High-level manager for state lifecycle, transitions, and manifest lookups."""
28|
29|    def __init__(
30|        self,

33|    ) -> None:

37|    @staticmethod

39|        normalized = dict(metadata or {})
40|        existing = normalized.get(STATE_MANAGER_METADATA_KEY)
41|        if isinstance(existing, dict):
42|            merged = dict(STATE_MANAGER_METADATA_DEFAULTS)
43|            merged.update(existing)
44|        else:
45|            merged = dict(STATE_MANAGER_METADATA_DEFAULTS)
46|        normalized[STATE_MANAGER_METADATA_KEY] = merged
47|        return normalized
48|
49|    def load_state(self, work_id: str) -> HarnessState | None:
50|        """Load the persisted state for ``work_id`` if present."""
51|
52|        return self._store.get_state(work_id)
53|
54|    def load_or_bootstrap_state(

57|        *,
58|        metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
59|        created_at: str | None = None,
60|    ) -> HarnessState:
61|        """Load state for ``work_id`` or create a deterministic default state."""
62|
63|        existing = self._store.get_state(work_id)
64|        if existing is not None:
65|            return existing
66|
67|        timestamp = created_at or self._now_provider()
68|        state = HarnessState(
69|            work_id=work_id,
70|            created_at=timestamp,
71|            updated_at=timestamp,
72|            metadata=self._normalize_metadata(metadata),
73|        )
74|        return self._store.put_state(state)
75|

1|"""Shared governed artifact contract definitions for the harness runtime."""

12|class ArtifactContract(HarnessModel):
13|    """Contract metadata describing a governed artifact type/version pair."""
14|
15|    artifact_type: ArtifactTypeV1 = Field(description="Governed artifact type")
16|    version: str = Field(default="v1", description="Contract version tag")
17|    description: str = Field(description="Human-readable description of the contract")
18|    required_fields: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Fields that must be present on the artifact")
19|    optional_fields: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Fields permitted but not required")
20|    evidence_required_fields: list[str] = Field(
21|        default_factory=list,
22|        description="Fields that require supporting evidence before verification",
23|    )
24|    verification_rules: list[str] = Field(
25|        default_factory=list,
26|        description="Rule identifiers or descriptions that govern verification",
27|    )
28|    approval_policy: str = Field(default="standard_review", description="Approval policy metadata")
29|    metadata: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict, description="Additional implementation-specific metadata")
30|
31|    @field_validator("version")
32|    @classmethod
33|    def version_must_be_tagged(cls, value: str) -> str:
34|        if not value.startswith("v"):
35|            raise ValueError("version must start with 'v'")
36|        return value
37|
38|    @field_validator(
39|        "required_fields",
40|        "optional_fields",
41|        "evidence_required_fields",
42|        "verification_rules",
43|    )
44|    @classmethod
45|    def entries_must_be_non_empty_and_unique(cls, value: list[str]) -> list[str]:
46|        if any(not item.strip() for item in value):
47|            raise ValueError("list entries must not be blank")
48|        if len(value) != len(set(value)):
49|            raise ValueError("list entries must be unique")
50|        return value
51|
52|    @field_validator("approval_policy")
53|    @classmethod
54|    def approval_policy_must_not_be_blank(cls, value: str) -> str:
55|        if not value:
56|            raise ValueError("approval_policy must not be blank")
57|        return value
58|
59|    @model_validator(mode="after")
60|    def validate_contract_shape(self) -> ArtifactContract:
61|        overlap = set(self.required_fields) & set(self.optional_fields)
62|        if overlap:
63|            raise ValueError(f"required_fields and optional_fields overlap: {sorted(overlap)}")
64|
65|        allowed_schema_fields = set(self.required_fields) | set(self.optional_fields)
66|        missing_schema_fields = set(self.evidence_required_fields) - allowed_schema_fields

FILE: harness_cost_guard (4690B) — /tmp/denuto/src/harness/cost_guard_middleware.py
1|"""
2|Cost guard middleware — budget-aware model downgrade for LLM calls.
3|
4|Reads cumulative cost from ``src/billing/cost_tracker.py`` before each LLM
5|call.  When the running total exceeds the configured threshold, it sets
6|``ctx.model_id_override`` to a cheaper model so the innermost handler can use
7|it.
8|
9|This is a *pre-call* middleware: the decision is made before ``next(ctx)`` is
10|awaited.  If no ``RequestCostTracker`` is active in the current context
11|(i.e., ``get_cost_tracker()`` returns ``None``), the middleware is a no-op and
12|lets the call proceed normally.
13|
14|Metadata written
15|----------------
16|``cost_guard.current_cost_usd``: float — cumulative cost at decision time.
17|``cost_guard.threshold_usd``: float — the configured threshold.
18|``cost_guard.triggered``: bool — whether the downgrade was activated.
19|``cost_guard.original_model_id``: str | None — model before downgrade.
20|``cost_guard.downgrade_model_id``: str | None — model substituted.
21|``cost_guard.skipped_reason``: str | None — if check was skipped.
22|"""
23|
24|from __future__ import annotations

FILE: harness_loop_detection (4369B) — /tmp/denuto/src/harness/loop_detection_middleware.py
1|"""
2|Loop detection middleware — break retry loops caused by repeated LLM responses.
3|
4|Tracks the MD5 hash of each response across invocations sharing the same
5|``session_id + agent_stage`` key.  If the same response hash appears a
6|second time, the middleware short-circuits subsequent retries and annotates
7|the context instead of calling the LLM again.
8|
9|This complements the existing ``CircuitBreaker`` (which handles provider-level
10|failures) by catching identical-output loops that the circuit breaker would
11|not detect: a stuck agent that returns coherent but wrong output on every retry
12|would not trip the circuit breaker but would waste tokens and time.
13|
14|Metadata written
15|----------------
16|``loop_detection.hash``: str — MD5 hex digest of the response.
17|``loop_detection.loop_detected``: bool — ``True`` when a duplicate was found.
18|``loop_detection.loop_count``: int — how many times this hash has appeared.
19|``loop_detection.skipped_reason``: str | None — if check was skipped.
20|
21|State
22|-----
23|Each ``LoopDetectionMiddleware`` instance tracks state per
24|``session_id:agent_stage`` key.  For multi-instance (Lambda) deployments the
25|check is local per-instance, which is sufficient for the common case of a
26|single retry loop within one Lambda invocation.
27|"""
28|
29|from __future__ import annotations
30|
31|import hashlib
32|import logging
33|from collections import defaultdict
34|
35|from src.harness.middleware import MiddlewareContext, NextFn
36|
37|logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
38|
39|
40|def _response_hash(text: str) -> str:
41|    """Return a short MD5 hex digest of ``text``."""
42|    return hashlib.md5(text.encode("utf-8"), usedforsecurity=False).hexdigest()
43|
44|
45|class LoopDetectionMiddleware:
46|    """Post-call middleware that detects repeated LLM responses.
47|
48|    On each call, the response hash is recorded for the
49|    ``session_id:agent_stage`` key.  If the same hash recurs, a warning is
50|    logged and ``ctx.metadata["loop_detection.loop_detected"]`` is set to
51|    ``True``.  The response is NOT replaced — callers decide how to handle
52|    the flag.
53|
54|    Args:
55|        max_occurrences: How many times the same hash may appear before the
56|            loop is considered detected.  Defaults to 1 (any repeat triggers
57|            the flag).
58|    """
59|
60|    def __init__(self, *, max_occurrences: int = 1) -> None:
61|        self._max_occurrences = max_occurrences
62|        # key: "session_id:agent_stage" → list of hashes seen
63|        self._seen: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
64|
65|    def _state_key(self, ctx: MiddlewareContext) -> str:
66|        return f"{ctx.session_id}:{ctx.agent_stage}"
67|
68|    async def __call__(self, ctx: MiddlewareContext, next: NextFn) -> MiddlewareContext:
69|        # Run the LLM call first (post-call middleware)
70|        ctx = await next(ctx)
71|
72|        if not ctx.response:
73|            ctx.metadata

1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""PermissionRequest hook: auto-approves known-safe Bash commands.

13|    # Testing

17|    "npx tsc --noEmit",
18|    "npx jest",
19|    "pytest",
20|    "python -m pytest",
21|    "python3 -m pytest",

29|    "git fetch",

33|    "tree ",
34|    "wc ",
35|    "head ",
36|    "tail ",
37|    "cat ",
38|    "file ",
39|    "which ",
40|    "command -v",
41|    # Package inspection
42|    "pip show",
43|    "pip list",
44|    "pip3 show",
45|    "pip3 list",
46|    "npm list",
47|    "npm ls",
48|    "npm outdated",
49|    "npm view",
50|    # Build
51|    "npm run build",
52|    "npx next build",
53|    # Formatting
54|    "npx prettier",
55|    "ruff format",
56|    "ruff check",
57|]
58|
59|
60|def main():
61|    try:
62|        input_data = json.load(sys.stdin)
63|    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
64|        sys.exit(0)
65|
66|    tool_name = input_data.get("tool_name", "")
67|    if tool_name != "Bash":
68|        sys.exit(0)
69|
70|    command = input_data.get("tool_input", {}).get("command", "").strip()
71|
72|    for prefix in SAFE_PREFIXES:
73|        if command.startswith(prefix) or command == prefix.strip():
74|            output = {
75|                "hookSpecificOutput": {
76|                    "hookEventName": "PermissionRequest",
77|                    "decision": {"behavior": "allow"},
78|                }
79|            }
80|            print(json.dumps(output))

FILE: block_dangerous (2659B) — /tmp/denuto/.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-commands.py
1|#!/usr/bin/env python3
2|"""PreToolUse hook: blocks dangerous shell commands before execution.
3|
4|Reads JSON from stdin with tool_name and tool_input.
5|Returns exit code 2 to block, 0 to allow.
6|"""
7|import json
8|import sys
9|import re
10|
11|DANGEROUS_PATTERNS = [
12|    # Destructive file operations
13|    r'\brm\s+.*-[a-z]*r[a-z]*f',       # rm -rf
14|    r'\brm\s+-[a-z]*r[a-z]*\s',         # rm -r (recursive delete)
15|    r'sudo\s+rm\b',                      # sudo rm anything
16|    r'\bchmod\s+777\b',                  # world-writable permissions
17|    r'\bchmod\s+-R\s+777\b',            # recursive world-writable
18|
19|    # Dangerous git operations on main/master
20|    r'git\s+push\s+--force\s+.*\b(main|master)\b',   # force push to main
21|    r'git\s+push\s+-f\s+.*\b(main|master)\b',        # force push to main (short flag)
22|    r'git\s+reset\s+--hard',             # hard reset (loses uncommitted work)
23|    r'git\s+clean\s+-[a-z]*f',           # git clean -f (deletes untracked files)
24|    r'git\s+branch\s+-D\s+main\b',      # delete main branch
25|    r'git\s+branch\s+-D\s+master\b',    # delete master branch
26|
27|    # System-level danger
28|    r'sudo\s+chmod\b',                   # sudo chmod
29|    r'mkfs\b',                           # format filesystem
30|    r'dd\s+if=',                         # raw disk write
31|    r'>\s*/dev/sd[a-z]',                 # overwrite disk device
32|    r'curl\s+.*\|\s*sh',                # pipe curl to shell
33|    r'curl\s+.*\|\s*bash',              # pipe curl to bash
34|    r'wget\s+.*\|\s*sh',               # pipe wget to shell
35|
36|    # AWS destructive operations
37|    r'aws\s+s3\s+rb\b',                 # remove S3 bucket
38|    r'aws\s+s3\s+rm\s+.*--recursive',   # recursive S3 delete
39|    r'aws\s+ec2\s+terminate-instances',  # terminate EC2
40|    r'aws\s+rds\s+delete-db-instance',   # delete RDS
41|    r'aws\s+cloudformation\s+delete-stack', # delete CFN stack
42|]
43|
44|def main():
45|    try:
46|        input_data = json.load(sys.stdin)
47|    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
48|        sys.exit(0)
49|
50|    if input_data.get('tool_name') != 'Bash':
51|        sys.exit(0)
52|
53|    command = input_data.get('tool_input', {}).get('command', '')
54|
55|    for pattern in DANGEROUS_PATTERNS:
56|        if re.search(pattern, command, re.IGNORECASE):
57|            msg = f"BLOCKED: Dangerous command pattern detected: {pattern}"
58|            print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
59|            output = {
60|                "systemMessage": f"Blocked dangerous command. Pattern matched: {pattern}. If you need to run this, ask the user for explicit confirmation first."
61|            }
62|            print(json.dumps(output))
63|            sys.exit(2)
64|
65|    sys.exit(0)
66|
67|if __name__ == '__main__':
68|    main()

FILE: consistency_scorer (10849B) — /tmp/denuto/src/pipeline/consistency_scorer.py
1|"""Consistency-sampled calibrated confidence for compiler findings.
2|
3|Research (`LLM_Legal_Contract_Analysis_Failure_Modes_Research.md` §10) shows that
4|self-reported LLM confidence is systematically overconfident (GPT-4 assigned its
5|highest confidence score to 87% of responses, including factually wrong ones)
6|and recommends consistency-based methods instead.
7|
8|This module runs N cheap re-verification calls against a lightweight model
9|asking a yes/no question — "Given this quote and context, does this finding
10|hold?" — then maps the agreement rate to a calibrated confidence score.
11|
12|The feature is shipped behind ``Config.enable_consistency_scoring`` (default
13|False) so it can be turned on in shadow mode or A/B testing before replacing
14|the compiler-LLM self-report as the routing signal.
15|"""

18|

20|import re

40|@dataclass
41|class ConsistencyScore:
42|    """Calibrated consistency signal derived from N re-verification votes.
43|
44|    ``agree_rate`` is the fraction of samples that returned ``yes`` — samples
45|    that error out or return ``null`` count as disagreement (conservative).
46|    ``calibrated_confidence`` is the agree_rate rounded to the fixed mapping
47|    in ``_AGREEMENT_TO_CONFIDENCE``.
48|    """
49|
50|    agree_rate: float
51|    calibrated_confidence: float
52|    sample_votes: list[str | None] = field(default_factory=list)
53|    sample_reasons: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
54|    model_id: str = ""
55|    n: int = 0
56|    error_count: int = 0
57|    latency_ms: int = 0
58|
59|    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
60|        return {
61|            "agree_rate": self.agree_rate,
62|            "calibrated_confidence": self.calibrated_confidence,
63|            "sample_votes": list(self.sample_votes),
64|            "sample_reasons": list(self.sample_reasons),
65|            "model_id": self.model_id,
66|            "n": self.n,
67|            "error_count": self.error_count,
68|            "latency_ms": self.latency_ms,
69|        }
70|
71|
72|# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
73|# Agreement-rate -> calibrated confidence mapping
74|#
75|# For N=3:
76|#   3/3 yes  -> 1.00   (unanimous agreement)
77|#   2/3 yes  -> 0.50   (split majority — weak signal, route to potential_issues)
78|#   1/3 yes

FILE: coverage_audit (7237B) — /tmp/denuto/src/pipeline/coverage_audit.py
1|"""
2|Post-compile coverage audit.
3|
4|For contracts with >=10 top-level clauses, verifies that every top-level
5|clause is referenced by at least one compiled finding. Clauses with zero
6|findings are surfaced as soft ``potential_issues`` so reviewers catch
7|"silent" omission failures — the CLAUSE benchmark's Perini Corp category
8|(see ``LLM_Legal_Contract_Analysis_Failure_Modes_Research.md`` §7).
9|
10|Default-off: called from ``src/entrypoint_core.py`` only when
11|``config.enable_coverage_audit`` is True.
12|"""
13|
14|from __future__ import annotations
15|
16|import re
17|from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
18|from typing import Any
19|
20|from src.pipeline.chunker import ClauseChunk
21|
22|# Threshold below which we do not bother emitting coverage warnings — signal
23|# to noise is too low on short deals and the primary path already reads them
24|# end-to-end without risk of middle-loss.
25|_MIN_CLAUSES_FOR_AUDIT = 10
26|
27|_ISSUE_LIST_KEYS = (
28|    "critical_issues",
29|    "high_issues",
30|    "medium_issues",
31|    "low_issues",
32|)
33|
34|_SYNTHETIC_RULE_NAME = "Coverage Audit: Silent Clause"
35|
36|
37|@dataclass
38|class CoverageReport:
39|    total_top_level_clauses: int
40|    covered_clauses: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
41|    silent_clauses: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
42|    skipped_reason: str | None = None
43|
44|
45|def _iter_top_level_chunks(clause_chunks: list[ClauseChunk]):
46|    """Yield ``(clause_id, heading, chunk)`` for top-level (depth <=1) chunks.
47|
48|    Skips synthetic entries like the preamble and the single-chunk fallback
49|    for short documents.
50|    """
51|    for chunk in clause_chunks or []:
52|        if chunk.clause_id in {"preamble", "whole_document"}:
53|            continue
54|        if chunk.depth > 1:
55|            continue
56|        yield chunk.clause_id, chunk.heading, chunk
57|
58|
59|def _issue_text_bundle(issue: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
60|    """Flatten issue fields into a single lowercased haystack for matching."""
61|    parts = [
62|        issue.get("verbatim_quote") or "",
63|        issue.get("rule_name") or "",
64|        issue.get("details") or "",
65|    ]
66|    return "\n".join(str(p) for p in parts).lower()
67|
68|
69|def _normalise_reference_tokens(chunk: ClauseChunk) -> list[str]:
70|    """Produce substrings the audit will look for inside issue text."""
71|    tokens: list[str] = []
72|    heading = (chunk.heading or "").strip()
73|    clause_id = (chunk.clause_id or "").strip()
74|    if heading:
75|        tokens.append(heading.lower())
76|    if clause_id and clause_id.lower() not in [t.lower() for t in tokens]:
77|        tokens.append(clause_id.lower())
78|    return tokens
79|

FILE: chunker (10732B) — /tmp/denuto/src/pipeline/chunker.py
1|"""
2|Clause-indexed chunking for long contracts.
3|
4|Mitigates the "lost-in-the-middle" / omission failure mode documented in
5|``LLM_Legal_Contract_Analysis_Failure_Modes_Research.md`` by giving downstream
6|consumers (re-analysis, coverage audit) stable, heading-anchored slices of
7|the extracted contract text.
8|
9|Default behaviour is OFF: nothing in the primary pipeline imports this module
10|unless ``config.enable_clause_chunking`` (or a flag that implies it) is True.
11|
12|The chunker intentionally does not alter how the structural agent emits its
13|findings. It accepts a light-weight ``ClauseHeading`` contract (see
14|``src/pipeline/chunker.py`` module docstring) and can also reconstruct
15|headings from raw text using the same regexes the structural agent uses.
16|"""
17|
18|from __future__ import annotations
19|
20|import re
21|from collections.abc import Iterable
22|from dataclasses import dataclass, field
23|from typing import TypedDict
24|
25|# Mirror the heading regexes from src/pipeline/agents/structural.py so the
26|# chunker does not depend on the structural module's internals.
27|_HEADING_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(
28|    r"^\s*(?P<kind>Section|Clause|Article|Schedule|Appendix|Appendices|Annex(?:ure)?|Exhibit|Part)\s+"
29|    r"(?P<token>[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9]+)*(?:\([A-Za-z0-9ivxIVX]+\))*)(?=[\s.,:;\-]|$)",
30|    re.IGNORECASE,
31|)
32|_HEADING_BARE_RE = re.compile(
33|    r"^\s*(?P<token>\d+(?:\.\d+)*(?:\([A-Za-z0-9ivxIVX]+\))*)\b(?=[\s.,:;\-]|$)",
34|)
35|
36|# Docs shorter than this get a single chunk — chunking buys nothing when the
37|# whole document already fits comfortably in a prompt.
38|_SHORT_DOC_THRESHOLD_CHARS = 4_000
39|
40|
41|class ClauseHeading(TypedDict, total=False):
42|    """Canonical clause-heading record consumed by the chunker.
43|
44|    ``char_start`` is required; everything else is inferred when missing.
45|    """
46|
47|    heading: str
48|    clause_id: str
49|    depth: int
50|    char_start: int
51|
52|
53|@dataclass
54|class ClauseChunk:
55|    """A contiguous slice of the extracted contract text anchored to a heading."""
56|
57|    clause_id: str
58|    heading: str
59|    text: str
60|    char_start: int
61|    char_end: int
62|    depth: int = 0
63|
64|
65|@dataclass
66|class ChunkStats:
67|    total_chunks: int
68|    total_chars: int
69|    coverage_ratio: float
70|    deepest_depth: int
71|    middle_chunk_count: int = 0
72|    middle_chars: int = 0
73|    headings_used: int = 0
74|    short_doc: bool = False
75|    details: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

FILE: discovery (14166B) — /tmp/denuto/src/pipeline/discovery.py
1|"""Post-compilation discovery pass -- finds 0-5 unusual risks outside the extraction schema.
2|
3|The discovery pass runs after the compiler produces its standard risk analysis.
4|An LLM reviews the full contract text for unusual/non-standard clauses that
5|the extraction schema does not cover, with mandatory verbatim quotes.
6|
7|Findings are deduplicated against existing compiled issues and unevaluable rules
8|using fuzzy title matching (80%) and fuzzy quote matching (85%).
9|
10|Exports:
11|    discovery_pass          -- Main entry point
12|    DiscoveryFinding        -- Pydantic model for a single finding
13|    DiscoveryFindings       -- Pydantic model wrapping list of findings (max 5)
14|    _deduplicate_discovery  -- Internal dedup function (exported for testing)
15|"""

38|class DiscoveryFinding(BaseModel):
39|    """A single discovery finding with mandatory verbatim quote."""
40|
41|    rule_name: str = Field(description="Short descriptive name for the finding")
42|    details: str = Field(description="Description of the unusual/non-standard clause")
43|    verbatim_quote: str = Field(description="Exact verbatim quote from the contract text")
44|    severity: str = Field(description="Severity: critical, high, medium, or low")
45|    recommendation: str = Field(default="", description="Recommended action")
46|    confidence: float = Field(default=0.6, ge=0.0, le=1.0, description="Calibrated confidence (0.0-1.0)")
47|    confidence_reason: str = Field(default="", description="Brief reason for confidence level")
48|
